conclusion: Earlier fixed-support papers in Six Birds Theory introduced admissible event packages, predictive quotients, and recombination witnesses. They left open whether a recombination-positive witness family supports a genuine promoted package or only a lower-layer summary. We answer that question on a frozen Route A corpus. We define a promotion criterion requiring sufficiency on the designated observable surface, induced update closure, admissible second-stage stability, control admissibility, protocol honesty, and slice legibility. The corpus is exact-finite and controlled: a two-anchor flagship core, four nearby positives, and matched null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls, together with a support-only erasure comparison surface. We replace an earlier vacuous second-stage rule with an admissible surface-coarsening audit and treat the artifact control in paired protocol-aware form. On this pipeline, an intrinsic candidate package survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, preserves the required control contrasts, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit. Two representative-selected route families also survive on the flagship core, but only as secondary evidence: they do not support a unique best strategy and they do not displace the intrinsic survivor. Slice/dual analyses are support-only and the staging–packaging defect atlas is explanatory. A Lean criterion kernel formalizes the promotion vocabulary and the generic implication from the criterion fields to promoted-package status. The resulting claim is narrow: at least one promoted-package candidate survives honestly on fixed support in the Route A flagship family.

conclusion: We ask whether a recombination-positive witness family supports a genuine promoted package or only a lower-layer summary. This section fixes the criterion vocabulary used throughout. The definitions are intentionally structural and route-family-level; they do not presuppose linearity, additivity, or a unique surviving package. Each individual field of the criterion has a recognizable neighbor in the existing literature; a consolidated positioning statement appears at the end of the section. [Candidate promoted package] Fix a common support surface together with a designated observable family and an admissible family of lower-layer operations. A candidate promoted package is an abstract package-level description intended to summarize lower-layer states or histories on that fixed-support surface. Its purpose is not merely to record a smaller state space but to provide a package on which the designated observables and admissible operations can be read without hidden dependence on arbitrary representatives. A candidate may be intrinsic, representative-selected, protocol-indexed, or otherwise structured, but it is always evaluated on the same frozen corpus and designated slice.

The induced update law is the package-level expression of descent from the lower surface.

conclusion: An admissible second-stage coarse-graining is a further package-level coarse-graining or repackaging that remains admissible relative to the retained observable surface and the induced update law. Not every quotient of the candidate is admissible; admissibility is tied to the structure the package is supposed to preserve. The identity coarse-graining is always admissible. The substantive question is whether nontrivial admissible further coarse-grainings exist and, if so, whether the decisive structure survives them.

conclusion: A candidate package counts as a promoted package on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold: [label=( )] Sufficiency. The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus. Induced closure. The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law. Second-stage stability. The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility. Control admissibility. The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way. No-smuggling. The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized. Slice legibility. On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{def:promoted-package-criterion}
A candidate package counts as a \emph{promoted package} on the designated corpus and slice only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item \textbf{Sufficiency.} The candidate supports the designated observable family on the frozen corpus.
\item \textbf{Induced closure.} The admissible lower-layer operations descend to a well-defined package-level update law.
\item \textbf{Second-stage stability.} The decisive structure survives admissible further coarse-graining, or else the candidate is rigid-minimal for explicit admissibility reasons rather than vacuous fragility.
\item \textbf{Control admissibility.} The candidate separates the required null, memory-only, artifact, and boundary-sensitive controls in the right way.
\item \textbf{No-smuggling.} The candidate's apparent success does not depend on omitted protocol or scheduler variables that should have been internalized.
\item \textbf{Slice legibility.} On at least one designated slice, the candidate is not merely sufficient but distinguished as a frontier-level package.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: A distinct case occurs when promotion is available only after context or protocol state is internalized into the package. We call this protocol-indexed promotion. The base candidate does not qualify honestly on its own, because its apparent success depends on omitted protocol state, but an internalized or explicitly indexed version satisfies the promoted-package criterion once that dependence is represented inside the state object. This is stronger than a mere artifact diagnosis and weaker than intrinsic promotion: the route remains live, but only as an indexed package rather than as a context-free one.

conclusion: The empirical and computational results above are carried by the fixed-support audit pipeline, not by theorem proving alone. We supplement them with a small formal layer that records a compile-checked definition package for the promotion criterion and a generic kernel theorem assembling the criterion fields into promoted-package status. The Lean development is not a mechanization of the full computational atlas. The implementation context is Lean 4 with the surrounding mathlib ecosystem . The development is organized around a generic promotion namespace. At the definition level, it formalizes the abstract notions used in : candidate promoted packages, induced update laws, admissible second-stage coarse-grainings, promoted-layer criteria, and protocol-indexed promotion criteria. These definitions are route-family-level. They do not encode repository artifacts, benchmark identifiers, or pipeline-level details; they make precise the logical shape of the criterion rather than reproduce the workflow inside Lean.

conclusion: The intrinsic route P_ int is the main result because it survives on both flagship anchors, covers the four nearby positives, separates the required controls, and remains honest under the paired artifact audit without requiring representative-selected correction. The representative-selected routes refine that picture rather than replacing it. They show that the surviving-package surface on the flagship core is richer than a single route, but their support remains route-family-level: they do not justify a unique best strategy claim, and they do not displace the intrinsic route. If P_ int had failed and only a representative-selected route had survived, the natural reading would have shifted toward a lift-selected or protocol-indexed package. That is not the current evidential state. Interpreted modestly, this intrinsic-versus-representative asymmetry is closer to familiar contrasts between intrinsic state abstraction, predictive state, and selected refinement than to a claim that one universal abstraction recipe has been proved . The support layers are easier to interpret when kept in their proper place. The slice/dual analysis shows that the surviving-route picture is not exhausted by a single scalar tradeoff ordering: different slices can favor different material route families. This is informative but remains support-only and provisional. The staging–packaging defect atlas contributes explanatory route geometry; it is not a classifier and not even positively ordered in the simplest positive-versus-control way. It sharpens interpretation without entering the claim-bearing pipeline.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The flagship-oriented witness stub does not claim that the actual Route~A flagship computation has been mechanized. It packages the assumptions a flagship-style survivor route would need in order to instantiate the criterion kernel, and so functions as an interface between the abstract criterion language and the route-family evidence used in the main text. The accompanying examples demonstrate that the definitions and kernel are usable on small formal objects; their purpose is pedagogical and sanity-checking, not empirical.
